Y82.tagline: One more title in green, then the coach walked out the door and the league traded everything that wasn't nailed down.

articles.headline: The Last Dance in New York
articles.dek: The Jets went 15-2, beat the Eagles in Super Bowl CXLI and handed Dorren Skura another title. Then the coach took the keys to Atlanta.
body: The Jets did what the Jets do under Dorren Skura. They finished 15-2, ran the bracket and beat the Eagles in Super Bowl CXLI. The final was 46-8. It was another Super Bowl title for the coach and New York's third in a seven-season run that also delivered CXXXVI in Y77 and CXXXIX in Y80.

The engine was Kane Van Oxley. The Ox added 145 catches, 2,496 yards and 39 touchdowns across 20 games in Y82, took the MVP and climbed into the S tier of the skill grades. Ty Lock threw for 4,909 yards and 61 touchdowns and walked off with the Super Bowl MVP. A first-year receiver, Vyncint Heath, caught 85 balls for 1,592 yards and was named Offensive Player of the Year. Up front, Jakeem Friend collected ring number 7.

Then the map changed. Before Y83 kicked off, the coach moved to the Falcons and took Van Oxley, Ryland Maxwell and Chance Woodrum with him, sending Malakai Sawyer back to the Jets. A wave of three- and four-way trades followed: Lock to the Giants, Van Oxley on to the Bears, Heath and Shareef London to Atlanta, Drake Wise through Atlanta and on to the Ravens, Dan Stout to New York.
One offseason was all it took to break up a champion. This is the story of the Y82 season, the last title of the Jets era, and the scramble that came after it.

articles.headline: Atlanta Calling, Then the Shuffle
articles.dek: The coach took three champions south and kept two. When the trades stopped, the Falcons were Heath, London, Maxwell and Woodrum, and The Ox was a Bear.
body: It started with the coach. Dorren Skura walked away from the champion Jets for the Falcons and took three of his title core with him: Kane Van Oxley, Ryland Maxwell and Chance Woodrum. Malakai Sawyer went the other way, back to New York.

That was only the opening act. Before a down of Y83, the league erupted in three- and four-way trades and Atlanta's haul changed shape. Kane Van Oxley, the reigning MVP, never played a game in red: he was flipped to the Bears. Drake Wise, brought in from the Giants for an unnamed quarterback, was a Falcon just long enough to be moved on to the Ravens. In came Vyncint Heath from the Jets and Shareef London from the Bears.

So the coach's first Falcons are Heath, London, Maxwell and Woodrum. Maxwell, 2 rings in 56 games and 1,430 rushing yards in Y82, is the back. Woodrum brings 3 rings and 931 tackles to a brand new secondary. London, 2,849 yards and 37 touchdowns in 86 games, gets a fresh start with a contender.
For Van Oxley it is pure whiplash: a title, an MVP, a ticket to Atlanta and then Chicago, all in one offseason. For Atlanta it is a reset built around the two Jets who stayed with their coach.

articles.headline: Champions Nobody Recognizes
articles.dek: The Jets kept the trophy. The coach, the MVP, the Super Bowl MVP and the Offensive Player of the Year all left. This is who is left to defend it.
body: Count what is gone from New York: Dorren Skura to Atlanta, Van Oxley to Chicago, Lock to the Giants, Heath to the Falcons, Maxwell and Woodrum with the coach. Half the roster that hung the CXLI banner has scattered.

What stays is the spine. Jakeem Friend, 7 rings and 526 blocks, still anchors the line. Jaylen Conklin, the tight end known as “Takeoff” for a vertical that lets him snatch anything thrown above his head, brings 4,502 yards and 66 touchdowns. Kalif Suh forced 4 fumbles in Y82 and sits at 10 for his career. Trequan Roberts, 2 rings, and rookie Dwayne Skura hold the secondary.

The new faces are familiar ones. Dan Stout takes over at quarterback, and Malakai Sawyer comes home: a Jet from Y76 to Y78 and a champion in Y77, he ran for 1,169 yards and 26 touchdowns for the Falcons last season and returns with 13,041 career rushing yards.
It should feel strange in New York this year. The banner is fresh, the faces are not, and Stout, ringless in 264 games, has just been handed a team that knows how to win one.

articles.headline: Three Quarterbacks, Three New Homes
articles.dek: The Super Bowl MVP is a Giant, the Ravens' starter now runs the champions' offense, and Drake Wise was a Falcon for exactly one trade.
body: Ty Lock leaves New York with 2 rings, 2 MVPs and a Super Bowl MVP from CXLI. His career line reads 22,189 yards and 239 touchdowns in 93 games, and the multi-team deals sent all of it to the Giants. Lock walks out a champion, the rare player who leaves on top.

His replacement is a volume passer still hunting a first ring. Dan Stout has thrown for 48,796 yards and 472 touchdowns in 264 games without one, and his Y82 in Baltimore added 3,055 yards, 26 touchdowns and only 4 interceptions. Now he inherits the defending champions, and with them the one thing his career has never had: a real shot at a ring.

Drake Wise took the strangest route. The coach traded an unnamed quarterback to the Giants to bring him to Atlanta, and the league-wide shuffle moved him on to the Ravens before he took a snap there. He arrives in Baltimore with 2 MVPs, 45,968 yards and 467 touchdowns, and like Stout, no ring. His Y82: 3,331 yards, 33 touchdowns, 3 interceptions.

articles.headline: The Ox and Heatwave
articles.dek: Kane Van Oxley played his way into the S tier. Vyncint Heath played his way onto the map in 17 games.
body: Van Oxley's Y82 was a highlight reel in numbers: 2,496 yards on 145 catches, 17.2 a catch, with 39 touchdowns. That is a touchdown on more than a quarter of his receptions. They call him “The Ox” for the strength that breaks tackles and holds up blocks, and no player Skura has coached has recovered more fumbles. The market caught on this year: his value went from 716 to 1,515, up 111.6%. He now carries 14,921 career yards, 147 touchdowns and 3 rings to Chicago, a Falcon for a moment and a Bear for real.

Heath was the surprise. In his first 17 games he caught 85 passes for 1,592 yards, 18.7 a catch, won Offensive Player of the Year and a ring, and debuted with a skill grade of A−. They call him “Heatwave”. The multi-team trades sent him to Atlanta, so he still plays for the coach who watched him break out, now beside Maxwell and Woodrum.

articles.headline: The Other Side of the Ledger
articles.dek: Not every stock went up. Two veteran receivers lost their bite and the market cooled on two defenders.
body: Juawan Lance has 4 rings and 15,422 career yards, but his Y82 season added 396 yards on 45 catches. That is 8.8 a catch for a receiver who averages 13.2 over his career. Craig Whitney caught 85 balls and turned them into just 442 yards, 5.2 a catch against a career 9.9, and his skill grade slipped to C−.

On defense, Darrel Longa logged 95 tackles in 17 games, yet his OVR dropped from 75 to 73 and his market value fell 22.5%. Taywan Tuttle's value dropped 43.5% without a new game played, the steepest fall on the market this season.
None of it erases a career. It does show which way these careers are trending.

articles.headline: Record Watch: Jensen Closes In
articles.dek: Trequan Jensen is one big season from Rondale Ikarras. The tackles race has a new name in it.
body: Ikarras holds the league's career rushing mark at 23,178 yards. Trequan Jensen sits at 21,690, 1,488 short, after a Y82 that added 1,390 yards and 19 touchdowns. One more season like that leaves him knocking on the door. He already has more career rushing touchdowns than anyone in league history, 388 to Ikarras's 374.

The tackles record belongs to Mose Junior at 2,862. Dan Mosley has 2,658 and added none in Y82, and Abraham Ward Jr has pulled to 2,653, right on his heels. Mosley also has 37 interceptions, 3 behind Jayon Queen's 40.
Kalif Suh forced 4 fumbles in Y82. That puts him at 10 for his career, one behind Tyrone Baugh's league-best 11.

articles.dek: Kirk Lenoir joined the 50,000-yard club, Ward Jr joined the Hall of Fame, and Jakeem Friend kept collecting jewelry.
body: Kirk Lenoir crossed 50,000 career passing yards with a Y82 that added 3,386 yards and 37 touchdowns. He now sits at 51,978, though his skill grade dipped to D+ on the way. Jason Macleone keeps climbing too: 73,799 yards, 771 touchdowns and 331 games, fourth on the career passing list.

Abraham Ward Jr passed 2,500 tackles and crossed Career Legacy 7,000, which makes him the Hall of Fame's Y82 class. The Packers defensive back has 2,653 tackles and 33 interceptions in 236 games, a Defensive Player of the Year and a ring.
Jakeem Friend won his 7th ring with the Jets and passed 500 career blocks, now 526 in 252 games. Linemen do not win MVPs. They win this.

articles.headline: Same Opponent, Different Uniform
articles.dek: Three Super Bowls against the Eagles, three wins, with three different clubs.
body: Philadelphia keeps finding Dorren Skura on the biggest stage, and it keeps ending the same way. He beat the Eagles 36-28 in CVIII with the Ravens in Y49, 38-11 in CXXXI with the Titans in Y72, and again in CXLI with the Jets. That is three meetings and three wins, each in a different uniform.

The thread runs through Malakai Sawyer. He was Rookie of the Year on that Y72 Titans team, the only season he ever spent in Tennessee, and he is the man the Jets got back when the coach left for Atlanta. If the Eagles get there again, they will meet a fourth Skura club: the Falcons.

articles.headline: Where Are They Now: The Ones Who Walked
articles.dek: Alvin Tufele retired, Dylan Hyatt left the league and Blair Iupati never played a down in green.
body: Before Y82 the Jets let two champions walk out the door, and a third never really arrived. Dylan Hyatt was not brought back and left the league. Alvin Tufele was let go too and has since retired. Blair Iupati came over from Seattle in a trade and was shipped on to New Orleans almost as soon as he landed.

Tufele came over from Seattle in the Obinna Leary trade, played Y81 for the Jets and is done: 230 games, 1,158 catches, 18,352 yards, 188 touchdowns and 3 rings. Hyatt leaves with 6 rings, 1,713 tackles and 231 games, his last club the Jets.
Iupati was a Jet for about as long as a trade call lasts. The Seahawks defensive back, 112 games and a ring, went on to the Saints before he ever suited up in New York.

Y83.tagline: A new club, a new quarterback, a new receiver in full flight, and the old champions waiting in the final.

articles.headline: Year One in Atlanta Ends With a Ring
articles.dek: The Falcons went 12-5, ran the table in the playoffs and beat the Jets 40-25 in Super Bowl CXLII. Dorren Skura's first season in red ended against the club he left.
body: Nobody gave the Falcons a bye. They finished 12-5, played their way in through the first weekend of the playoffs and did not lose again, finishing 40-25 over the New York Jets in Super Bowl CXLII. It was another title for Dorren Skura, won in his first season with a new club, against the champions he had coached a year earlier.

The offense belonged to people who were not in Atlanta a year before. Brandon Jaclyde, in his first 21 games in the league, threw for 5,199 yards and 56 touchdowns and was named Most Valuable Player. Vyncint Heath, the receiver they call "Heatwave", turned a trade into the best season of his young career: 137 catches, 2,504 yards, 34 touchdowns and the Super Bowl MVP. Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,919 yards and 25 scores and won Offensive Player of the Year.

The defense was new too. Simeon Otton was Rookie of the Year at linebacker, Jashaun Fleming worked the line, and Trysten Floyd joined Chance Woodrum in the secondary. Woodrum, one of the three champions who followed the coach south, now owns 4 rings.

On the other sideline stood the club Skura built. Malakai Sawyer and Jaylen Conklin carried the Jets back to the final, and lost to Skura on Super Bowl Sunday, as New York has every time the two have met in the final.

The celebration did not last long. Before the second season in Atlanta began, Shareef London went to Tampa Bay for Shawn Milne, Jaclyde was traded to the Dolphins and Perrion Randall to the Seahawks. The champions are already a different team.

articles.headline: Jaclyde: One Season, One MVP, One Ring, One Trade
articles.dek: Brandon Jaclyde threw 56 touchdown passes in his first 21 games, won the MVP and the Super Bowl, and was a Dolphin before his second season began.
body: A year ago the quarterback question in Atlanta was a revolving door. Drake Wise came and went in a single trade, and the Falcons opened Y83 with a passer who had never taken a snap in the league. Brandon Jaclyde answered it emphatically.

In 21 games he threw for 5,199 yards and 56 touchdowns, about two and a half scores a game, and took the league's Most Valuable Player award. His 26 interceptions say he never stopped taking shots, and with Heath running past people, most of those shots landed. He also ran it in 4 times.
The skill grades rate him in the A band already. The market is slower: his card opened at a value of 19, a long way below the established passers he outplayed.

Then the business side arrived. Before the Falcons' second season, Jaclyde was traded to the Dolphins. Miami gets a reigning MVP with one season on his card, and Atlanta goes looking for its third starting quarterback in three offseasons.

articles.headline: Heatwave Takes Flight
articles.dek: Vyncint Heath caught 137 passes for 2,504 yards and 34 touchdowns, then took the Super Bowl MVP. His skill grade climbed to A+.
body: Last season "Heatwave" was a promising rookie with 85 catches on a loaded Jets roster. This season he was the reason defensive coordinators lost sleep.

Heath played all 21 Falcons games and caught 137 passes for 2,504 yards and 34 touchdowns. That is 18.3 yards a catch on a season's worth of volume, and a touchdown on roughly one of every four receptions. When the Falcons needed one more play in Super Bowl CXLII, it went his way, and so did the game's MVP award.

Two seasons in, he has 2 rings, an Offensive Player of the Year award and a Super Bowl MVP. The skill grades moved him from A- to A+, and his card value jumped 262 percent. The ceiling is not in sight yet.

articles.headline: Maxwell Carries the Load, and the Hardware
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,919 yards and 25 touchdowns, won Offensive Player of the Year and added a third ring.
body: Ryland Maxwell was one of the three champions who followed Skura out of New York, and he made the move look like a promotion. In Atlanta he was the every-down back: 1,919 rushing yards and 25 rushing touchdowns across 21 games, plus another 10 catches out of the backfield.
The league noticed. Maxwell was named Offensive Player of the Year, the first individual award of his career beyond his Rookie of the Year trophy, and the Super Bowl win gave him 3 rings in 77 games.

The market has been slower to catch up. His skill grade sits at C+ and his card value of 20 is modest for a back with his resume, which makes him one of the better bargains on the board heading into the second Atlanta season, where he remains on the roster.

articles.headline: The Rest of the Roster Nobody Knew
articles.dek: A rookie of the year at linebacker, an S-grade lineman and a tight end who scored on almost a quarter of his catches.
body: Champions are remembered by their stars, but this Falcons team was built out of first-year cards. Eric Raimann caught 54 passes for 792 yards and 13 touchdowns at tight end. Perrion Randall was credited with 58 blocks in 21 games on the line and debuted with a skill score of 99, the top of the S tier.

On defense, Simeon Otton made 94 tackles at linebacker and was named Rookie of the Year. Jashaun Fleming matched him with 94 tackles and added 3 sacks up front. Trysten Floyd made 62 tackles, picked off a pass and forced a fumble in a secondary anchored by Chance Woodrum, who added 117 tackles and a fourth ring.
Every one of them now has a ring in his first season. Not all of them will wear red in the next one: Randall was traded to the Seahawks before the second Atlanta season.

articles.headline: Beating the Team He Built
articles.dek: The defending champion Jets made it back to the Super Bowl with Skura's old core. Skura has still never lost a Super Bowl to New York.
body: The Jets did not collapse after the coach left. With Dan Stout running the offense, Malakai Sawyer back in green and Jaylen Conklin still catching everything thrown above his head, New York returned to the final. Sawyer ran for 1,844 yards and 37 touchdowns, Conklin added 122 catches for 908 yards and 9 scores, and Kalif Suh made 54 more tackles.
It was not enough. The Falcons won 40-25, and Skura stayed unbeaten in Super Bowls against the Jets, now with yet another club.

The market still rated the losers' season. Conklin's card value rose 313 percent, the biggest jump in the league, even as his skill grade slipped from A+ to A. Sawyer's grade rose to B+ and his card value climbed 80 percent. Suh's card value tripled. The roster that won CXLI is still good enough to win another; it simply ran into the coach who assembled it.

articles.headline: Champions, Then Sellers
articles.dek: Shareef London went to Tampa Bay for Shawn Milne, Jaclyde to Miami and Randall to Seattle before the second Atlanta season.
body: Shareef London's Atlanta chapter lasted one season. He arrived from the Bears in the Y83 multi-team trades, caught 91 passes for 1,579 yards, won the first ring of his career, and was then shipped to the Buccaneers for Shawn Milne before the second Falcons season. London leaves with 45 career touchdowns and a card value that rose 50 percent in his year as a Falcon.

He was not the only champion out the door. The MVP, Brandon Jaclyde, was traded to the Dolphins. Perrion Randall, an S-grade lineman after one season, was traded to the Seahawks, the club Skura's Jets beat in Super Bowls CXXXVI and CXXXIX.

What remains in Atlanta is the spine: Heath, Maxwell, Woodrum and the young defense of Otton, Fleming and Floyd, with Raimann at tight end. The coach has rebuilt on the fly before. He will have to do it again in year two.

articles.headline: Where the Old Jets Landed
articles.dek: Ty Lock found his footing with the Giants, Drake Wise posted 38 touchdowns in Baltimore and The Ox spent his first season as a Bear outside the playoffs.
body: Last offseason's trades scattered the Jets' stars around the league. One season later, the returns are in.

Ty Lock played 19 games for the Giants, a playoff appearance included, and threw for 3,678 yards and 33 touchdowns. The skill grades cooled on him slightly, from A+ to A-. Drake Wise, who passed through Atlanta on paper only, threw for 3,496 yards and 38 touchdowns for the Ravens in 19 games, and his card value rose 33 percent.

Kane Van Oxley had the quietest year of the three. "The Ox" played 17 games for the Bears with no postseason, catching 58 passes for 909 yards and 8 touchdowns. His skill grade slipped out of the S tier to A+.

articles.dek: Trequan Jensen retired after Y83 with the rushing record still in Rondale Ikarras's hands. The tackles chase belongs to Dan Mosley, with K'Lavon Settle coming.
body: For two seasons the question was whether Trequan Jensen had one more big year in him. He played Y83 and then retired, and the career rushing record still belongs to Rondale Ikarras. Through Y82, Jensen had 21,690 rushing yards, 1,488 short of the mark; his final season's line was never recorded, but the record did not change hands.
That leaves the tackles chase as the league's headline pursuit. Dan Mosley's latest card holds 2,658 tackles, 204 behind Mose Junior's record.

The name to watch behind him is K'Lavon Settle. He added 238 tackles in 17 games, climbed to 2,356 for his career and moved up to an 89 overall with an A- grade. At that pace the tackles leaderboard will have a new name near the top within a few seasons.

articles.headline: Market Report: Winners, and Two Backs in Free Fall
articles.dek: Conklin, Iupati and Tim Wright more than tripled their card values. JR Bashaam and Tramon Amerson lost nearly half of theirs.
body: The card market rewarded production this season. Jaylen Conklin's value rose 313 percent, Blair Iupati's 300 percent after 474 tackles in 34 games since his last card, and Tim Wright's 283 percent on the back of 2,871 rushing yards and 64 touchdowns across 37 games.

The other side of the ledger belonged to two running backs who did not get a new card. JR Bashaam's value fell 46 percent as his OVR slid from 69 to 65, and Tramon Amerson's fell 42 percent with a drop from 71 to 68. Jake Gano, a defensive lineman, lost 22 percent.
The lesson of the market is the lesson of the league: the cards that move are the ones that keep playing.

articles.headline: Three Veterans Walk Away
articles.dek: Dan Stout, Jakeem Friend and Trequan Jensen all played Y83 and retired when it ended.
body: The offseason after the Falcons' title took three long careers with it.

Dan Stout quarterbacked the Jets in his one season in New York, all the way to Super Bowl CXLII, after a long career in Baltimore. He retires without a ring. Through Y82 he had thrown for 48,796 yards and 472 touchdowns against just 51 interceptions.

Jakeem Friend walks away a seven-time champion on the offensive line. He had 7 rings and 526 blocks across 252 games through Y82, most of those seasons spent in Seattle, and he finished his career in green.
Trequan Jensen retires a Packer, with 21,690 rushing yards and 388 rushing touchdowns through Y82 and the Y79 title on his resume.
Their final Y83 lines were never recorded, so the careers above stand as the books through Y82.

Y84.tagline: A record season on the ground, a second straight title in Atlanta won with key pieces missing time, and two new names in the Hall of Fame.

articles.headline: Atlanta Does It Again
articles.dek: The Falcons went 13-3-1 and held off the Broncos 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII, carried by a record season from Ryland Maxwell and two first-year players who left with rings.
body: The Falcons are champions again. Atlanta finished the regular season 13-3-1, survived a four-point final against the Denver Broncos, 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII, and gave Dorren Skura a third straight title: one with the Jets, now two with the Falcons. A roster that was torn apart and rebuilt after the first ring simply did it again.

This one was won on the ground. Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,272 yards and 27 touchdowns, the best rushing season the record board has ever shown, and finished the job as Super Bowl MVP. He played all 20 games of the run and now owns 4 rings in 97 career games.

The passing game belonged to a newcomer. Orlando Larienne, in his first season, threw for 3,485 yards and 41 touchdowns and left with a ring. He appeared in only 15 of the 20 games, and a team that also saw Vyncint Heath miss time still found a way. Heath, the receiver they call "Heatwave", caught 119 passes for 2,209 yards anyway and won a second Offensive Player of the Year award.

Up front, Calais Ham made 49 blocks in his first season and has a ring to show for it. Shawn Milne, who came from Tampa Bay in the trade that sent Shareef London the other way, won the first of his career, and Chance Woodrum now has 5.

Up the coast, the old club had a milestone of its own. Malakai Sawyer ran for 1,551 yards for the Jets and crossed into the Hall of Fame, the only member of its Y84 class. In Los Angeles, the Rams' Von Horsted crossed the same line, though he has since fallen out of the Hall. The Falcons kept winning.

articles.headline: Maxwell Runs Into the Record Book
articles.dek: 2,272 rushing yards in one season, a Super Bowl MVP and a fourth ring before his hundredth game.
body: No back on the record board had ever had a season like it. Ryland Maxwell carried the Falcons for 2,272 yards in Y84, the new mark for the best rushing season, and added 27 rushing touchdowns plus 4 more as a receiver. He did it in every one of Atlanta's 20 games, the one constant on a roster that had to cover for missing pieces elsewhere.

It was a jump even from the year he won Offensive Player of the Year, when he ran for 1,919. His career now reads 7,705 rushing yards and 102 rushing touchdowns in 97 games, and the season pushed him past 100 rushing scores.

The market noticed. His card rose from an overall of 67 to 75 and from a C+ grade to B+, and its value went from 20 to 112. With 4 rings and a Super Bowl MVP before his hundredth game, Maxwell has stopped being the back who followed the coach from New York. He is the reason Atlanta keeps winning.

articles.dek: Orlando Larienne played 15 of Atlanta's 20 games and Vyncint Heath played 18. The champions won anyway.
body: The Falcons' two most productive passing pieces were not always on the field. Orlando Larienne, a first-year quarterback, appeared in 15 of the club's 20 games, missing 5. Injury cost him those games. When he played, he was devastating: 41 touchdowns against 13 interceptions, better than three scores for every pick. His card opened in the A+ tier.

Vyncint Heath missed 2 games, a year after playing all 21 of Atlanta's first title run. The games he lost to injury barely showed in the numbers. In 18 games he caught 119 passes for 2,209 yards and 22 touchdowns, 18.6 yards a catch, and took his second Offensive Player of the Year award. His card climbed into the S tier, its overall from 70 to 77.
Both finished with rings. For a team that had to keep winning with a starter or a star in street clothes, that may be the most telling number of all.

articles.headline: Green Bay Finds Its Back
articles.dek: Angelo Moton ran for 1,717 yards and 31 touchdowns and was named Rookie of the Year for the Packers.
body: Angelo Moton did not ease into the league. In his first 20 games for the Packers he ran for 1,717 yards and 31 touchdowns, and the Rookie of the Year award went to Green Bay. His 31 rushing scores matched what Malakai Sawyer, a new Hall of Famer, managed for the Jets in the same season.
There is one thing to clean up. Moton also put the ball on the ground more often than a back of his talent should, the kind of habit that decides playoff games.

He had help. Solomon Toohill played all 20 games at quarterback and threw for 3,845 yards and 41 touchdowns with 5 interceptions, his card rising from an overall of 66 to 70. Toohill already has a ring from Green Bay's 44-6 win over the Chiefs in Super Bowl CXXXVIII. With a back like this behind him, the Packers have reason to think about another.

articles.headline: Sawyer Stands Alone in the Y84 Hall Class
articles.dek: A back who keeps running for the Jets crossed Career Legacy 7,000. A Rams safety who never left Los Angeles crossed it too, but his place did not last.
body: The Y84 class has 1 member, and it is Malakai Sawyer. Sawyer, in his second season back with the Jets, ran for 1,551 yards and 31 touchdowns in 19 games, passed 15,000 career rushing yards and reached a Career Legacy of 7,101. He ended Y84 with 16,436 rushing yards and 299 rushing touchdowns in 243 games, 2 rings and 2 Offensive Player of the Year awards.

Von Horsted got there too, one tackle at a time. A Ram since Y70 and nothing else, he played all 17 games, made 231 tackles, 13.6 a game, and intercepted 2 passes. That lifted his career to 2,658 tackles and 33 interceptions in 254 games and his Career Legacy from 6,833 to 7,345. His card's value rose from 3,118 to 4,806. His Career Legacy has since slipped below the mark the Hall asks its earlier members to hold, and he is no longer part of the class.
Sawyer's résumé is rings and records. Horsted's is a Defensive Player of the Year award and a body of work built entirely in one uniform. Only one of them is still in the Hall.

articles.dek: Jimmy Tillery was intercepted only 4 times in his first season. Ty Lock, the old starter, is a Giant now.
body: The club Skura left behind went with youth at quarterback. Jimmy Tillery played all 19 of the Jets' games in his first season and threw for 3,392 yards and 27 touchdowns, with only 4 interceptions. He was not explosive, but he was careful, and careful kept the Jets in games.

He had a Hall of Famer behind him in Malakai Sawyer and a familiar target in Jaylen Conklin, the tight end they call "Takeoff", who caught 85 passes for 513 yards. Kalif Suh played all 19 games on defense.

Across town, Ty Lock is a Giant now, traded there from the Jets in the multi-team deal before Y83. He played 18 games and threw for 3,204 yards and 24 touchdowns with 2 interceptions. Lock owns 2 rings and 2 MVP awards. Tillery has a long way to go to match that, but the start was clean.

articles.headline: Life After Atlanta
articles.dek: Brandon Jaclyde, Shareef London and Perrion Randall left the champions after one season. All three spent Y84 watching their old club win again.
body: The Falcons traded away three pieces of their first title team, and none of them got a second ring. Brandon Jaclyde, the reigning Most Valuable Player, went to Miami and threw for 2,807 yards and 26 touchdowns with only 2 interceptions in 17 games for the Dolphins. Solid, but a long way from the 56 touchdowns he threw as a Falcon.

Shareef London's road ran from the Bears to Atlanta in the multi-team deal before Y83, then on to Tampa Bay in the trade for Shawn Milne. He caught 61 passes for 464 yards and 5 scores with the Buccaneers, 7.6 yards a catch. Milne, meanwhile, collected the ring.

Perrion Randall played 17 games for the Seahawks and was credited with 16 blocks. His card actually climbed, its overall from 66 to 74, even as his grade fell from the S tier to B+. For all three, Atlanta was a single season, a single ring, and then a view from somewhere else.

articles.headline: Denver Meets Skura, and Loses, Again
articles.dek: Four Super Bowls against the Broncos, four wins, with three different clubs across 68 seasons.
body: The Broncos have now reached the final against Dorren Skura four times and lost every one. The first came in Y16, a 22-16 win with the Commanders. Two more followed with the Buccaneers, 46-11 in Y23 and 38-16 in Y25. Then nothing for nearly six decades, until Atlanta beat Denver 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII.

This was the closest of the four by a distance. The first three were decided by six points or more, two of them by more than three touchdowns. Denver had a four-point game and a tight end with a long memory: D.C Paradis, who has 995 career catches, played all 20 games of the Broncos' run and is now five catches short of a thousand.
For Skura it is a rivalry measured in eras. The Commanders, the Buccaneers dynasty and now the Falcons have all taken their turn, and the Broncos are still waiting for their first win.

articles.headline: Four Straight for Skura, and Atlanta Has Never Looked Better
articles.dek: The Falcons went 15-2, beat the Bengals in Super Bowl CXLIV and gave Dorren Skura another title behind a record season from Ryland Maxwell.
body: The Falcons are champions for a third straight season, and Dorren Skura has now won four titles in a row across two clubs. Atlanta went 15-2 in the regular season, beat the Cincinnati Bengals in Super Bowl CXLIV and added another championship to Skura's career.

It was the most complete season of the run. The 15-2 mark was the club's best since Skura arrived, two wins better than last year's 13-3-1, and Atlanta played 20 games in all on the way to the trophy.

Ryland Maxwell was the engine again. He ran for 2,617 yards and 39 touchdowns, breaking his own single-season rushing mark and the rushing touchdown record on the same board, and added the best rushing game it has ever recorded, 237 yards. He won his second Offensive Player of the Year award and his fifth ring.

The new piece was a rookie. Apollo Adam caught 85 passes for 1,654 yards and 18 touchdowns in his first season and was named Super Bowl MVP. Orlando Larienne, who missed time a year ago, played in all 20 games and threw 51 touchdown passes. Vyncint Heath, the receiver they call "Heatwave", added 2,059 yards.
Around the league, the Jets' Jimmy Tillery was named Most Valuable Player and Seattle's Deonte Sutton took Defensive Player of the Year. In Atlanta, the only question left is how long this can last.

That carried him past 10,000 career rushing yards. He now has 10,322 of them and 141 rushing touchdowns in 117 games, with 5 rings and 2 Offensive Player of the Year awards.

The market moved with him. His card went from an overall of 75 to 79 and from a B+ grade to A minus, and its value rose 150.9%, from 112 to 281. The room had already changed: Shawn Milne, a champion in Atlanta in Y84, was traded to the Giants at the start of the season, and Heath carried the veteran load, playing all 20 games and catching 106 passes for 2,059 yards. The question now is not whether Adam belongs, but how much more there is.

The final belonged to the Falcons' newest and oldest weapons. Apollo Adam, a rookie, was named the game's Most Valuable Player. Ryland Maxwell closed a season in which he broke three records. For Cincinnati, a franchise that has now been stopped by the same coach with two different clubs, the wait for a first win over Skura goes on.

The rings kept stacking up. Chance Woodrum collected his seventh, Maxwell his sixth. Around the league, Kalif Suh of the Jets crossed into the Hall of Fame and K'Lavon Settle of the 49ers took over the career tackle lead. articles.headline: Philadelphia Rises: Skura Takes the Eagles to the Super Bowl CXLVII Title
articles.dek: In his first season in Philadelphia, Dorren Skura led the Eagles to a 14-2-1 record, past Atlanta and Green Bay, and to a 40-22 win over the Broncos.
body: A new city, a new roster and the same ending. Dorren Skura left Atlanta after five straight championships, took over the Philadelphia Eagles, and won again. The Eagles finished the regular season 14-2-1, beat the Falcons and the Packers at home in the playoffs, and handled the Denver Broncos 40-22 in Super Bowl CXLVII.

It is the Eagles' first title since Y4, when they also beat Denver, 36-28. In between, Philadelphia lost five Super Bowls, the last of them a 46-8 defeat by Skura's own Jets in Y82. The coach who handed the Eagles that loss has now delivered the parade.

The quarterback was a newcomer. Bones Crawford, on his first card, threw for 5,922 yards and 69 touchdowns, then was named Super Bowl MVP. His favorite targets were two receivers built for volume. Vyncint Heath, acquired from Atlanta, caught 140 passes for 2,204 yards and 28 touchdowns and won his third Offensive Player of the Year award. Kaulani Rahman, another new card, added 2,247 yards on 124 catches.

The road ran straight through Skura's old house. Atlanta, still led by Ryland Maxwell, reached the playoffs and met the Eagles in Philadelphia, and the Eagles ended the Falcons' title run there. Green Bay, with Most Valuable Player Solomon Toohill, fell the same way a round later.

Two losses, one tie and a championship in the first year of a rebuild is a remarkable debut. For Skura it is something more familiar: one more season that ended with a trophy, this time in a third city.

articles.headline: Bones Crawford Arrives With 69 Touchdown Passes and a Super Bowl MVP
articles.dek: The Eagles quarterback put up one of the great debut cards in league history: 5,922 yards in 20 games.
body: Few quarterbacks on a card have opened a career like Bones Crawford. In his first 20 games he threw for 5,922 yards and 69 touchdowns, and he capped the season as the Super Bowl MVP in Philadelphia's win over Denver.

The profile is aggressive. Crawford averaged 296 passing yards and more than three touchdown passes a game, a quarterback who attacks downfield and trusts his receivers to win the ball, and the cost was 26 interceptions. On an offense with Vyncint Heath and Kaulani Rahman, that bargain paid off week after week.

The market has not caught up yet. His card opens at an overall of 62, because overall rewards a long career, but his skill grade is already an S. If the next seasons look anything like this one, that overall will not stay low for long.

articles.headline: Heath for Adam: The Receiver Swap That Shaped the Season
articles.dek: Philadelphia sent Apollo Adam to Atlanta for Vyncint Heath, and Heath answered with a third Offensive Player of the Year award.
body: The biggest trade of the offseason sent one star receiver each way between Skura's old club and his new one. Apollo Adam, the two-time Offensive Player of the Year, went from Philadelphia to Atlanta. Vyncint Heath, "Heatwave", came the other way.

Heath made the deal look lopsided. He caught 140 passes for 2,204 yards and 28 touchdowns, won his third Offensive Player of the Year award and added his seventh ring. His card's overall climbed from 86 to 90, and its value rose 115%.

Adam was good, not great, in his first Atlanta season. He caught 71 passes for 1,123 yards and 20 touchdowns, and he appeared in 18 of the Falcons' 19 games, so injury cost him time. His card's value still rose 73%, and the market clearly expects the best of his career to be ahead of him. The Eagles took the win in the playoff meeting, but this trade will be judged over several seasons, not one.

articles.headline: Spector Scores 35 in Houston After the Ogbah Trade
articles.dek: The Eagles moved Siran Spector to the Texans for Gerrit Ogbah. Both backs had good years, and both teams can claim the deal.
body: Philadelphia's other offseason swap was in the backfield. Siran Spector went to Houston and Gerrit Ogbah came to the Eagles, and the results split neatly along the lines of what each club needed.

Spector was a touchdown machine for the Texans. He ran for 1,533 yards and 35 touchdowns in 19 games and caught 17 passes, and his skill grade rose from a B to an A minus. Houston did not get back to the final, but it found a back who finishes drives.

Ogbah gave the champions balance rather than headlines. He ran for 1,051 yards and 12 touchdowns, caught 27 passes for 185 yards and 4 more scores, and collected the first ring of his career in Super Bowl CXLVII. With Bones Crawford throwing for 5,922 yards, the Eagles did not need a workhorse. They needed a back who kept defenses honest, and Ogbah did that for 20 games.

articles.headline: The Falcons Run Ends Where the Coach Went
articles.dek: Atlanta still had Ryland Maxwell and a playoff team. It did not have Skura, and its run of titles ended in Philadelphia.
body: For five seasons the Falcons were the league's standard, champions every year from Y83 through Y87. Then the coach left, and the first team to stop Atlanta was the one he went to coach.

The talent did not disappear. Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,403 yards and 23 touchdowns in 19 games, his card's overall rose to 97 and his Career Legacy climbed to 8,057. Apollo Adam arrived from Philadelphia and scored 20 touchdowns. The Falcons made the playoffs and traveled to Philadelphia with a real chance.

They lost there, and the drop in Maxwell's numbers tells part of the story. A year after his record 2,670-yard season he gained a little more than half that total. A defense that no longer had to fear the threat of a historic season may have keyed on him; age and a new offensive rhythm may also have played a part.
Atlanta remains dangerous. But for the first time since Y82, Atlanta finished a season without the trophy.

articles.headline: Toohill Wins a Second MVP and Brooker Takes Defensive Honors
articles.dek: Green Bay collected two of the season's biggest awards before the Eagles ended its year in the playoffs.
body: Solomon Toohill is now a two-time Most Valuable Player. The Packers quarterback threw for 4,522 yards and 43 touchdowns against only 4 interceptions in 20 games, the second straight season he paired heavy volume with almost no mistakes. His card's value jumped 345%.

His teammate in the secondary had a breakout of his own. Jamon Brooker made 259 tackles and intercepted 6 passes and was named Defensive Player of the Year, adding to the Rookie of the Year award already on his card. His skill grade rose to an A and his card's value climbed 241%.

The Packers had the league's best regular-season quarterback and its best defender, and they still came up one round short again, beaten by Philadelphia in the playoffs. Green Bay has the pieces. It keeps running into Dorren Skura.

articles.headline: McClain and Orzech: Two One-Club Linemen Enter the Hall
articles.dek: The 49ers and Cowboys defensive linemen both crossed Career Legacy 7,500, and McClain finished the season one tackle from a record.
body: The Y88 Hall of Fame class belongs to the trenches. Aqib McClain of the 49ers and Keion Orzech of the Cowboys, two defensive linemen who have spent their whole careers with one club, both pushed their Career Legacy past 7,500.

McClain is the more remarkable case. He finished Y88 with 1,363 career tackles, one fewer than Lloyd Queen's 1,364, the most by any defensive lineman on a card, and he had made them at a faster pace. He added 97 tackles this season, and his card's value more than doubled, up 113%.

Orzech came into the league as Rookie of the Year and by the end of Y88 had made 1,296 tackles in 271 games. His signature is unusual for a lineman: 6 career interceptions, more than any of the great tacklers at his position.
Neither had won a ring. Both now have a place in the Hall.

articles.headline: Back to Back: Skura's Eagles Win Super Bowl CXLVIII
articles.dek: Philadelphia went 14-2-1 again, won three playoff games at home and beat the Bengals 44-14 for Dorren Skura's 64th title.
body: The second season in Philadelphia looked a lot like the first, and that is the highest compliment available. The Eagles finished 14-2-1 for the second straight year, earned a bye through the wild card round and then won three home games in a row: 46-24 over the Panthers, 32-28 over the Rams and 44-14 over the Cincinnati Bengals in Super Bowl CXLVIII.

The title is the 64th of Skura's career. Cincinnati arrived as a 10-6-1 club that had survived the AFC bracket, and it never found a foothold. The Rams game was the only real scare of the postseason, a four-point margin in a conference final that Los Angeles kept close to the end.

On the road, Philadelphia was untouchable. The Eagles went 8-0-1 away from home, the only blemish a 40-40 shootout in Dallas. Both defeats came at home: 33-30 to Washington, a loss that ended a 14-game winning streak stretching back into Y88, and 46-30 to Tampa Bay, the biggest upset of the season by record.

The stars were the same names that carried the first title, only better. Bones Crawford threw for 6,302 yards and 72 touchdowns and was named Most Valuable Player. Kaulani Rahman caught 145 passes for 2,635 yards and won Offensive Player of the Year. Vyncint Heath caught 28 touchdown passes and was the Super Bowl MVP for the second time in his career.
Two seasons in Philadelphia have produced two parades. The rest of the league is running out of ways to describe Skura, and running out of time to catch him.

articles.headline: Bones Crawford Follows a Record Debut With an MVP Season
articles.dek: The Eagles quarterback threw for 6,302 yards and 72 touchdowns in his second season and has 141 touchdown passes in 40 games.
body: A year ago the question about Bones Crawford was whether a debut like his could be repeated. He answered it by improving. In 20 games he threw for 6,302 yards and 72 touchdowns, up from 5,922 and 69, and the league named him its Most Valuable Player.

His style has not changed. Crawford still attacks down the field, averaging 16.8 yards per completion across his career, and he still accepts the risk that comes with it: 27 interceptions this season. With receivers who win the ball in the air, that bargain has now paid off twice.

Kaulani Rahman made the case that the quarterback had help. The second-year receiver caught 145 passes for 2,635 yards and 22 touchdowns, won Offensive Player of the Year and saw his card's value rise 122%.

Crawford's card moves more slowly. Its overall rose from 62 to 64, because overall rewards a long career, but his skill grade remains an S, and through 40 games he owns 141 touchdown passes and two rings.

articles.headline: Heath for Adam, Year Two: An Eighth Ring and a Second Super Bowl MVP
articles.dek: Vyncint Heath caught 28 touchdown passes for the champions. In Atlanta, Apollo Adam's numbers fell and the Falcons missed the playoffs.
body: The trade that sent Apollo Adam from Philadelphia to Atlanta and brought Vyncint Heath, "Heatwave", the other way now has a second chapter, and it reads much like the first.

Heath caught 123 passes for 2,414 yards and 28 touchdowns, was named Super Bowl MVP for the second time and collected his eighth ring. He did it in 18 of the Eagles' 20 games, so he missed 2 through injury. His card's overall rose from 90 to 93, his skill grade reached an S and its value climbed 67%.

Adam's second Falcons season went the other way. He caught 58 passes for 393 yards and 4 touchdowns in 17 games, a long way from the 1,123 yards of his first year in Atlanta, and the Falcons finished 9-8 and out of the playoffs. His skill grade slipped from an A to an A minus, though the card's value still rose 18%.
Two seasons in, Philadelphia holds two titles and the clear edge in the deal. Atlanta is still waiting for the version of Adam that won two Offensive Player of the Year awards.

Ogbah, for his part, has a second ring. He ran for 662 yards and 7 touchdowns and caught 21 passes for the champions.

The playoffs were less kind to Houston. The AFC place in Super Bowl CXLVIII went to Cincinnati, a 10-6-1 team, and the Texans were left with the best record in football and nothing to show for it. articles.headline: Washington, the Neighbor Philadelphia Cannot Shake
articles.dek: The Commanders ended a 14-game winning streak and are the only club to beat Skura's Eagles twice.
body: Every great team has a fixture it dreads, and for these Eagles it is Washington. The Commanders finished 7-10, a losing team by any measure, and still came to Philadelphia in week 8 and won 33-30. The defeat ended a 14-game winning streak that had begun in week 14 of Y88, the longest run in the weekly scores.

Across two seasons the Eagles have one win, two losses and a tie against Washington, the tie a 40-40 game in Washington in Y88. The Eagles did win the rematch this year, 30-20 on the road, but no other club has beaten them twice, and the Giants and Cowboys, the rest of the division, have not beaten them at all.

The other home loss had less history behind it and more shock. Tampa Bay, a 6-11 team, won 46-30 in Philadelphia in week 16, the biggest upset of the season by record and the most points the Eagles allowed all year. Two home defeats to two losing teams, set against a perfect road sheet: Philadelphia went 8-0-1 away.

articles.headline: Teamer Enters the Hall, McClain Takes the Tackle Mark, Horsted Drops Out

Aqib McClain, inducted a year ago, finished the chase he was one tackle short of. The 49ers lineman made 83 tackles in Y89 and now has 1,446, the most by any defensive lineman on a card, ahead of Lloyd Queen's 1,364. Keion Orzech, his classmate, retired this offseason with 1,296.
One member left. Von Horsted, the former Rams defensive back, saw his Career Legacy slip from 7,358 to 7,235, under the floor that members must hold, and he is no longer in the Hall.

In Super Bowl CXLIX the streak finally met a team built to end it. The Houston Texans beat Philadelphia 32-22, and Skura's title count stays at 64.

Houston arrived as the best team in football for the second year in a row. The Texans went 16-1, finished first in the power rankings again and, unlike a year ago, carried that form all the way through the playoffs. Philadelphia, second in the rankings, could not close the gap on the biggest stage.

The Eagles had done everything asked of them to get there. They won their first eight games, finished 14-3 and were perfect at home, 9-0 in the regular season. All three defeats came on the road: 36-22 at Dallas, 33-32 at the Rams and 28-24 at Washington. They allowed 360 points, the fewest in the league, and their point differential of 203 was the best of any club, a hair ahead of Houston's 196.

The postseason ran through Philadelphia. The Eagles beat the Rams 38-32, avenging the one-point loss in Los Angeles, and held off Green Bay 24-21 in the conference final. Bones Crawford, the league's Most Valuable Player for the second straight year, threw for 5,327 yards and 61 touchdowns. It is the first Super Bowl Skura has lost since Y74, when Hamsfa Boltt's Titans beat his Seahawks in CXXXIII. That was a long time ago. Houston has made sure the next chapter in Philadelphia begins with something to prove.

Ogbah, for his part, had his best season in Philadelphia. He ran for 1,137 yards and 14 touchdowns and caught 23 passes, 9 of them for scores, in all 20 games. It was not enough in the final.

The Super Bowl series between Skura and Houston now stands at 3-1. Houston lost two of those finals to Skura's Falcons, in Y86 and Y87. This time the trophy went to Texas, and the back Philadelphia let go was holding it.

body: Bones Crawford is two for two. The Eagles quarterback threw for 5,327 yards and 61 touchdowns and was named Most Valuable Player again, and in the process he passed 200 career touchdown passes. He now has 202 in 59 games.

He did it in 19 of Philadelphia's 20 games, so he missed one. Injury cost him the game he missed. The risk in his game has not gone away either: he threw 23 interceptions. His card's overall rose from 64 to 74, but his skill grade slipped from an S to an A plus.

Kaulani Rahman was the reason the offense never stalled. He caught 126 passes for 2,495 yards and 24 touchdowns, 19.8 yards a catch, and won Offensive Player of the Year for the second time. His card has gone from an afterthought to one of the hottest on the market: its value rose 2170%, and his grade climbed to an S.
Three seasons in, the pair has two rings, four of the league's top individual awards across the last two years and one Super Bowl defeat to answer for.

articles.headline: Calvin Wingo II Fills the Biggest Hole in Philadelphia
articles.dek: With Vyncint Heath gone, the rookie caught 120 passes for 2,218 yards and was named Rookie of the Year.
body: The question in Philadelphia this year was who would replace Vyncint Heath, the Super Bowl MVP of Y89, who did not play a down in Y90 and has since retired. The answer was a first-year receiver nobody had seen on a card before.

Calvin Wingo II played all 20 games, caught 120 passes for 2,218 yards and scored 16 touchdowns, 18.5 yards a catch. The league named him its Rookie of the Year, and his skill grade opened at an A plus.

He is not Heath yet. Heath scored 28 touchdowns in his last season, and Wingo's longest catch went for 40 yards: he piles up steady chunks rather than home runs. But a rookie who gives Crawford a second target of that volume changes how defenses line up against Rahman, and it helped the Eagles score 563 points.
The market has not caught up: the card opened at an overall of 67. That will not last long if Y91 looks anything like Y90.

articles.headline: Washington Splits Again as the Eagles Lose Only on the Road
articles.dek: The Commanders went 13-4 and won the rematch in week 16. The Rams beat Philadelphia by a point in the regular season, then lost to the Eagles in the playoffs.
body: A year ago Philadelphia was unbeatable away and vulnerable at home. In Y90 the pattern flipped. The Eagles went 9-0 at home and 5-3 on the road, and every one of the three defeats was a trip.

Washington again stood out. The Commanders were no longer a losing team: they went 13-4, finished third in the power rankings and split the series once more. Philadelphia won 30-28 at home in week 11; Washington won 28-24 at home in week 16. Across three seasons the Eagles are 2-3-1 against the Commanders, the only club in the division with a winning record against them.

The other two losses came out west and in Texas. Dallas, an 8-8-1 team, won 36-22 in week 10, the most lopsided defeat of the year. The Rams won 33-32 in week 12. Both debts were repaid: the Eagles beat the Cowboys 48-25 in week 17, and they beat the Rams 38-32 in the divisional round.

articles.headline: Diggs Retires, and a Broncos Card Takes His Touchdown Record by One
articles.dek: Danny Diggs left with 408 rushing touchdowns. Lane McCoy arrived with 409, and Tim Wright passed 350.
body: Danny Diggs spent the last few seasons pushing the career rushing touchdown record further out of reach. He retired after Y90 without playing a game in it, leaving with 408 scores, 21,421 yards and no ring.

Then the new rosters arrived, and with them a Denver back nobody had tracked. Lane McCoy of the Broncos carries 409 career rushing touchdowns, one more than Diggs, and 21,940 yards in 290 games. He is also the closest active back to Rondale Ikarras and the yardage record, 1,238 behind.

Tim Wright is the chaser now. The Rams back ran for 1,574 yards and 29 touchdowns in 19 games, passed 350 for his career and reached 354, still 55 short of McCoy. His Rams also handed the Eagles a 33-32 loss in week 12. His card's value rose 131%.
Isaiah Karras, now with New England, added 20 scores and passed 300, finishing at 315.

articles.headline: No Hall of Fame Class in Y90, but Stidham Is at the Door
articles.dek: Terron Stidham passed 3,000 tackles and sits just under the bar. Damar Hobbs arrives 3 interceptions from Daren Teamer's record.
body: For the first time since Y83, a season ended without a new Hall of Famer. It will not stay that way for long. Terron Stidham of the Ravens made 198 tackles in 18 games, passed 3,000 for his career and finished at 3,132. His Career Legacy rose to 7,470, just under the 7,500 bar, and he is now 53 tackles from K'Lavon Settle's career record.

The full rosters added three more names near the line. Damar Hobbs, a Patriots defensive back, arrived with a Career Legacy of 7,336 and 39 career interceptions, 3 short of the record Daren Teamer took into retirement this year. Quenton Fuller of the Chargers, at 7,279, and Tanner Tuttle of the Cardinals, at 7,251, are defensive linemen with long careers and no ring between them.
None of the four has a Most Valuable Player award or a Defensive Player of the Year trophy. All of them are close enough that one more full season could settle it.

articles.headline: Heath, Diggs, Teamer and Seven More Walk Away
articles.dek: Ten veterans are retired, among them a two-time Super Bowl MVP, the career interceptions leader and an eight-ring defensive back.
body: Vyncint Heath, "Heatwave", leaves at the top. He won 8 rings, 3 Offensive Player of the Year awards and 2 Super Bowl MVPs, the second in his last game, and caught 891 passes for 16,483 yards and 180 touchdowns in 153 games.

Daren Teamer, last year's only Hall of Fame inductee, retires with 2,740 tackles and 42 interceptions, the most on any card, and still no ring. Danny Diggs and Cairo Colbert, two backs who spent years near the top of the rushing tables, retire with 408 and 314 rushing touchdowns.

Hamsfa Boltt quarterbacked the Titans to Super Bowl CXXXIII in Y74 and was its MVP, and he finishes with 48,211 passing yards. Chance Woodrum, who followed Skura from the Jets to the Falcons, retires with 8 rings and 1,635 tackles.
Shawn Milne, Jarred Beasley, Tristan Tart and Niles Swoopes complete the list. None of the ten played a game in Y90.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: Around the league in Y90, the first season with every club's roster on file.
body: Jamon Brooker of the Packers made 210 tackles and won his second Defensive Player of the Year award; Green Bay's season ended 24-21 in Philadelphia.
Jacksonville went 2-15 and still produced the upset of the year, 47-43 at Buffalo, a 13-4 team.
Buffalo beat Tennessee 61-58 in week 7, 119 points, the most combined in the weekly scores; Carolina's 65 at Atlanta is the most by one club.
Xavier Mosley of the Raiders ran for 1,691 yards and 30 touchdowns, and Angelo Moton of the Packers also scored 30.

New colors at season's end: Keaton Toney with the Falcons after Tampa Bay, Kyron Atwell and Deshone Bello with the Jets after Atlanta, Rodger Samuel and Treyvon Scott with the Steelers after Green Bay.
Atwell made 212 tackles in 17 games; Raphael Mosely of the Rams made 213 in 19.
Dwayne Skura played 13 of the Eagles' 20 games, missing 7 through injury. Bryant Zappe played 17.

didYouKnow.text: The Eagles went 9-0 at home in Y90 and all three of their losses came on the road, the reverse of Y89, when both losses came at home.
Philadelphia allowed 360 points in Y90, the fewest in the league, and still finished second in the power rankings behind 16-1 Houston.
Bones Crawford has 202 touchdown passes and 2 MVP awards in the first 59 games of his career.
Lane McCoy has 409 career rushing touchdowns and no ring.
Calvin Wingo II caught 120 passes for 2,218 yards in his first 20 games, 6 a game.
Tim Sweeney threw 36 touchdown passes and only 4 interceptions for the champion Texans.
Nydair Sample of the Bengals has played 381 games and thrown for 70,168 yards, with 1 ring.
